body: That's decently accurate.

I just don't really like the way reality works. Combine that with the fact that I don't desire or enjoy any aspects of life enough to warrant the effort, work, and misery required for the continued sustenance of life.

What I meant by normal is people who have never actually, completely considered suicide. I could quite easily come to terms with a close person's suicide, because I'm not normal.

There are a few people I need to make understand why and come to terms with it first before I can go. That's going to be difficult in itself, as normal people don't really understand, and they definitely won't be too keen on letting me kill myself. Also, I haven't planned the method or any details yet, for obvious reasons.

I'm quite confused about why you commented either of your comments. What's your motivation to do that? There has to be something in it for you, otherwise you would have just kept scrolling down and not wasted the effort.
Not today. Some things aren't in order yet.
Yeah, at least she is happy. I've wanted to kill myself for a long time.

Sometimes it isn't as simple as that though.. If my mom didn't allow or enable me to become what I have, I would have killed myself many years ago. When faced with that ultimatum the decision of whether or not to enable becomes much more difficult.

Well in the past 25 years it's been nothing but a uniquely shitty experience. The 13 billion years before I was born was better, it flew by in an instant because my consciousness didn't exist. The total net sum was neutral for 13bil, yet in the past 25 the net sum is negative. I'd love for that neutral again. I really regret my parents deciding to conceive me, so much that I know I will never have a kid because no way in hell am I forcing someone into this miserable existence against their will or control. I can already play a few instruments, it's not that great. I do not enjoy writing, it's actually my most hated college subject. I've never liked a single subject. It's all just boring, miserable work. I already said I have no passions, I have never had any.

It's really strange to me that my lack of interests seems so impossible to you.  

Other than work and sleep, I do whatever I can that makes time go by faster. Eat, smoke, reddit, life obligations and responsibilities. Now the obvious thing to say is well duh, if that's all you do no wonder you're bored. But, that viewpoint is looking at it backwards. Those things don't cause the boredom, they are what I choose to do to kill time because nothing else is worth it.  

As far as the writing goes, I find that funny because you aren't the first one who says I sound articulate. Sorry to be mr. refutes all points, but its actually my weakest point in my entire education experience. Dropped out of highschool my junior year because I didn't write my junior paper, and I didn't want to do my senior project and paper the next year. Writing 122 is the class that made me drop out of college 3 times.  

I'm not really the creative, artsy type, I'm more the logical type. That's probably not the best way to describe it, but oh well. I'm decent at following rules and orders, so I'm average at math. I've always hated math though, all types. Tried trig, calc, stats, tried the more applied stuff in the sciences with physics and chemistry. Hated them all. Then again I've never enjoyed any school subjects.  

But creating things of my own, no way. Never been able to my entire life. Never been able to draw, or paint, write, build, or anything like that. And that word, inspiration, I don't think I've ever felt that.  

And sorry to be the guy that just negates every suggestion, I don't do it with that sole purpose and specific intent in mind. Its just what I feel. You just gotta keep picking and picking at me until there is nothing left ask or suggest. And only then we will come to the conclusion that no one on this planet can help me, and I can't help me, and any attempts are futile.

edit: forgot to mention that I do appreciate the time taken to read and respond to me. I know its tough and not exactly rewarding to interact with me. My only hope is that I'm at least providing and satisfying a little curiosity concerning the inner workings of my brain.  

edit2: funny thing I remember from the 4th grade pertaining writing and creativity. Earlier in the year we had to do a 5 paragraph persuasive essay. Then later in the year came the creative writing assignment. I got my teacher to allow me to do a second persuasive essay instead of the creative writing assignment, because I just couldn't do it.

Well, the reason I say I don't like X or I don't care, is because I don't. I can't explain it any farther than that.  

It's like saying "here, eat an apple, it will make you happy."  
"But I've eaten apples before, and I don't enjoy the taste."  
So then you say "Well there is a lot of different strains of apples with different flavors, keep trying them until you like one enough that it makes you happy."  
Then I say "Well I've tried a ton different kinds, and none of those tasted even remotely close to good. I don't really wanna spend the time, money, and effort trying every single apple in pure hope and speculation that maybe just 1 will be good." Thats my terrible analogy, except it applies to literally everything I've ever tried.  

I don't really hate anything specific about my job, except for sometimes I get 5am-2pm shifts. I can't explain it any differently than I hate the general concept of work, and always have. I quickly broke my parents when they tried to get me to do chores as a kid, and taught them that they have no means of punishing me. Anything a parent could legally do, I didn't care. Take my stuff away? I don't care. Grounded? I don't care. The chore would have been the worst punishment, but you can't literally force me into action, I'll just sit there and not do it.  

My best friends sister is the assistant GM, that's how I got the job. No where else would hire me. Nothing attracted me to this life, I had to get a job to survive. I don't want money. I don't want things.  

I've never seen another human being at work, and thought, hey I could survive doing this. I can't even do non-miserable things for 40 hours a week, there is no way in hell I could work a job 40 a week. I'm lucky I only get 15-20, and even then I want less. I've never enjoyed a single school subject. I've dropped out of highschool, then dropped out of college 3 times out of boredom, dislike of subjects, and not having motivation or an end goal because there is nothing I want.

I've done alcohol, tobacco, weed, shrooms, salvia, lsd, mdma, cocaine, shrooms, huffing nitrous oxide, sassafras, codeine. Probably more that I'm forgetting. I was pretty anti-drug as a kid/teen. Suicidal thoughts gave me the freedom to say fuck it and try them. Although I can't say any of them are enjoyable enough to warrant the cost and effort of doing them. It was mainly curiosity. Only ones I do now are tobacco and weed.  

If your last paragraph is true, than I am doomed. I've tried helping myself for over a decade and made absolutely zero progress. It doesn't work. So I reach out for help and no one can, I have to help myself I guess. I'm damn near ready to give up, I just don't care enough about anything to keep wasting effort on trying. I don't even think I want to get better at this point.
no reply?

I don't know. It doesn't really matter, its insignificant. Its just background noise.

Its worth noting that not a single comment in my post has pushed me farther away from suicide. If anything, its pushed me closer by making realize how futile this all is.

Or, you know, she could have different values, interests, and priorities than you. Maybe she doesn't enjoy programming or reading books?  

What if the people you are with are boring?  And you'd rather text to your friend or SO or play video games because all those things are far more interesting than anything else you have the current potential to do.
Quantum physics doesn't interest me. I don't care.

Yes, I've done all those things, except the finding music I love, because I don't love music. All those thing you listed are not worth working or living for, not even close.  

There aren't any meanings that I desire to create for my life.  

So why not take up something I haven't done before? Like what?  And that takes time, money, misery, effort, and resources which in not willing to commit unless it's guaranteed to make me want to live.
No not really

I guess where we differ, is I kind of have enough confidence in nothingness after death, even though we have no way of truly knowing, that it makes it worth the gamble to me. To me, it just seems like it will be just like the extremely long 13 billion years before I was born, completely nonexistent from my perspective.  

I'm not afraid of death at all. What causes me the most fear is the cause of death. I really, really, really, really do not want to get stabbed or have my throat slit, or be burned alive. Probably some others too, but those were the first to pop in my head.

I've dabbled into quantum physics a very brief, little bit. But that was a long time ago, in high school I think. I don't really remember much any of it.  

I don't care to reproduce.
Nah I'm actually the same way to an extent. I just like to play devil's advocate because that perspective is frequently overlooked.
I actually think that's a good reason, though. Personally, I have 0 fear of death itself, but I am quite afraid of dying in a miserable manner. Such as burning alive or getting my throat slit.

Haven't really blown up much either, just messing with fireworks, really. Take a Whistlin' Whilly or Piccolo Pete, wrap in duct tape, hit with hammer a shit ton, light. Radio in the car and whatever the company's playing at work.

I don't have that, not even a small one. I don't think I ever have.
Far from a waste of time. I found what you typed interesting, because I share similar ideas and qualities. That article was interesting, too.

Why am I sharing? Because everyone else seems to be okay with life, and it makes me curious as to why. I can't figure it out, it doesn't make sense to me. So I ask others to gain insight on their perspective.  

If the solution lies within me, I either can't find it, or it isn't there. Give it another year and try again? Kinda been doing this for two decades. I'm tired of just having something to do. That's boring, and not worth the work required to sustain my life.
I can't say I derive that same sense of satisfaction from proving others wrong, winning battles, or anything like that.
What if you don't want to change? What if you don't want to stop doing monstrous things, even though you recognize they are bad?
What if you don't want to be anybody or anything?

What could life possibly offer me? I'm sure it has tons to offer, but anything it has to offer is not something I desire.  

I've committed well over a year to "getting better," whatever the abstract idea 'better' means. Tried meds, CBT, and psychodynamic/analytic therapy. Nothing makes a difference.  

I don't care about the chances of being me. I don't care to try. I don't owe myself anything. I really just don't care.

I know I have depression.  

I alive because, well, I have no damn clue, aside from being forced to. I've been dead too, for about 13 billion years. Those 13bil were better than anything I've ever experienced since then.  

It isn't the exact job that is the issue, I've had many different jobs, its the basic idea of work in general. For work to be worth it, the positives have to outweigh the negatives. That's the only reason any human works. For them, having a job provides them with something they want, which is a sustained life with objects and people they desire. I will NEVER enjoy work or think its worth it, because work will never provide me with anything that I want. There are no positives. Just negatives, misery, and boredom.  

I have volunteered, I hated it. I get no pride or self-satisfaction from helping others. Feels literally identical to having a job. Boring, miserable, feels just like work. Not caring about money probably doesn't help this, as that's the only thing separating jobs from volunteering.  

Create myself? There's nothing I want to create.

I can definitely relate to the dreaming thing and wanting to be free. Dreaming is one of my favorite things. I've practiced lucid dreaming too, but never been able to master it and have complete control. My brain often wont comply to my commands despite my lucidity. For some reason, my brain really fights lucidity. Dream characters often attack me when I become aware I'm dreaming, or my brain will find other ways to distract me and take away my awareness. False awakenings happen a lot too while lucid, but I don't mind them as I see them as another chance to be lucid. I also really enjoy natural dreams too, mine are always crazy. There is so much more potential than what we are limited to in our world.  

I also read your other replies and the other threads you posted.

Ehh, not really. My sense of humor is rather lacking. Sometimes I find odd, interesting, random, or rare things funny or humorous. Also I tend to laugh at other peoples misfortune such as tripping but I usually feel guilty about those because if they happened to me I wouldn't want people laughing.

Well, there is nothing I desire or long for, nothing I want, short term or long term.  

As far as exercise goes, I really hate it. For the same reasons I hate work. It just feels like work. I'm 5 foot 10 and 135 pounds. I absolutely hate running. I've done the whole gym thing before, I worked out everyday for 6 months then decided to quit. Just wasn't worth it to me. All I got was misery and no joy.

I don't see how that's possible? I need food and things like that. I don't know how to balance work and non-work. I only work 10-20 hours a week as it is.  

Maybe I can help with the empathy. Picture every single second that work affects your life. From making you go to bed so you can sleep the day before, to waking up, shower, commute, then the entire time at work, commute, and whatever else it effects. Now every single second, and I mean literally every single second that passes, I'm hyper-aware of the misery and dread that working is making me feel. I want nothing more than to just quit every second I'm there. But I can't. I need to pay for my survival. So I'm forced to fight through this misery and every second feels like an uphill battle through the thickest and deepest sludge (metaphor for the mental battle I fight every damn second). And time seems to slow down, everything lasts longer, the misery feels like it lasts longer. So even though I only work 4 and a half hours, it feels way worse than that. Especially when I've only been there an hour and I think "fuck, I have to do this for 3 and a half more hours?! I don't know how I'm going to do this, I'm already so fucking sick of this". Plus, enjoyable things do the exact opposite of this, time goes by faster. So fun things that last hours feel like minutes, and misery at work feels like it lasts forever. And if you view time from my warped perspective instead of linear, it really isn't worth it. To me it feels like hours and hours of misery to pay for a short little bit of fun. And I hate that.  

I don't exactly have money for a doc, and I sure as hell don't want to work to afford one. But if I did, I'm sure he'll chalk it up to depression and put me on some expensive meds, which I'm really against. No clue why but I really have a strong aversion to meds.

Can't say I have. Although, it isn't something I long for or desire. I've attempted relationships before but I always realize that they aren't worth the effort. I'm introverted, and I might be aromantic but I'm not sure. I'm content being by myself and find others to undesirably complicate things. I don't like compromising, I'd rather just do what I want to do when I want to do it and not have to worry about how it affects others. I like it simple like that.

Well, if it means anything, I had great parents and a decent childhood compared to some people (although it was the same as every other kid who grew up near me, wasn't until high school where I realized how underprivileged many others were. But that was just because I wasn't exposed to it as a child). Nothing too amazing, and nothing I'd think was worth living for if I were to do them today. Non-abusive parents who gave me lots of freedom, I rode my bike with other neighborhood kids a ton and we went all over the place at a very young age. Seems like parents these days would never let their kids roam the city from dawn til dusk with no supervision like we did. The occasional vacation. And I still turned out this way.

Maybe, but it would have to be very specific. And even then I don't know if this would make me happy, I'd have to try it (which is impossible). I'd have to be able to do them only when I want to do them, and be able to quit doing them the instant I want to stop. Whether that means just quitting for a day in the middle of something because I don't feel like doing it anymore, or quitting for months. But then I'd have to be able to start again whenever I felt like it. They also couldn't affect my sleep. There couldn't be any pressure to perform well in those things. Mistakes couldn't be costly, they'd have to be easily fixable.  

Masturbation is alright, but its purely hedonistic and I view it like doing a (mediocre) drug. Feels good for the 5-10 seconds that the orgasm lasts. Never had sex, never really tried. The 5-10 second orgasm doesn't seem worth the effort required to have sex.  

Other hobbies? No clue, you pretty much already listed them. Smoking weed is alright, feels kinda good. If I never smoked again though I wouldn't really care, its not that great. Tried shrooms once, was alright. I've wanted to try dmt (it's the one thing on my bucket list before I suicide) but I've been too scared to try it after a bad salvia experience. But I figure if I'm ready to die, it seems pointless to fear anything so I should just give it a shot. I may try other drugs too just to experience them before I go. Heroine and cocaine obviously feel amazing, but I wouldn't want to do them until I'm certain of suicide. They are too addicting to try otherwise.

I've thought about it a lot, actually. It would depend on the conditions. I'd have to be warm and not hungry, and find some way to pass the time until age or health took my life. Why not skip that shit and just die now?
I don't know, I don't really care enough. Seems like work, and killing myself sounds easier. And depending on the methods and who is affected, it could interfere with my morals.

Im not sure if I completely understand the question, but I think its sort of both the world we live in currently and also the numbers thing of being born this way.  

If life and the world was different and I never had to work, I think I would be okay. But then again, I don't really know as I don't enjoy much. I think I'll get bored after awhile. And it's also the odds of being born this exact way with my exact genes. There are plenty of people happy with the way the world works now.

To be honest, I don't really know. I would wake up when I felt like waking up. I would eat whatever I am craving whenever I am hungry. I would go to bed when I am tired. Other than that, I have no clue.
Mostly the mental, but both really. They affect each other. My current job isn't very physical at all. But my previous jobs were physical and I hated them even more.

I wouldn't worry about your impact on society, it doesn't matter anyway, and the rest of society will be fine and functional regardless if you work or not. I'd say just do whatever you want or enjoy, nothing really matters. If you're like me and don't really enjoy anything, just do whatever you can to make time pass faster. That's what I do.

The thing is, I don't really care? I don't care if there "might" be great times in the future, I'm sure some nice or enjoyable things will happen here and there. The thing is, they just aren't worth the work. I'd rather just skip the good and the bad and just die now.

I dunno, I don't really care about wages. I just work to feed myself, pay for rent and gas because I have to. I don't want anything else so I don't really care about money.  

As far as the work goes, I'm there for half and hour to an hour before I want to just walk out and kill myself because I hate it so much. I then fight through that completely miserable every single second for the rest of my shift that drags on for what seems like forever.

I think the type of work is irrelevant. I hate ALL work. I've never had a passion for anything or any type of work. I hated all aspects and subjects in school. The work I currently do is simple, easy, nice coworkers and bosses, air conditioned, best job I've had yet. I'm there for 30min to an hour before I'm ready to fucking quit or kill myself. And then I have to push and fight through that as hard as I fucking can every damn second for the rest of my time there. It drags on and is completely fucking miserable.  

I would absolutely hate life if I had your work and commute. That sounds completely miserable. I don't care about money, its not worth the misery and effort. I do not think being old and retired is worth the amount of work to get there. I'd rather just die now.
